scope: The standing museum cut into the Derwent peninsula, including its concrete and rust-colored south face, terraced roof and Courtyard House entrance, ferry stair approach, and the adjoining Pharos and Round House envelopes.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: The architects identify the three-level gallery excavated below the former Moorilla estate, its concrete and corten shell, terraced green roof and stair linkage from the ferry landing.
The construction engineers record the 17-metre drop from the entrance to the gallery, and the 140 m long excavated northern wall.
The Tasmanian heritage inventory identifies the adapted Courtyard House entrance, Round House, original excavated museum and connected modern pavilions.
The architects describe the separate western Pharos volume and its cantilevered end over the Derwent.
